# zerops_service_restart (Resource)

Explicit restart invocation. Changing triggers replaces this resource and restarts once; unchanged applies do nothing. Restart starts a STOPPED service and may conflict with a sibling service desired_state=STOPPED. Delete is state-only and leaves the service running. Import is unsupported because triggers cannot be recovered. Do not put secrets in triggers.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "zerops_service_restart" "app" {
  service_id = zerops_service.app.id
  triggers = {
    # Reference the completed env resource to order its write before restart.
    # Use a nonsecret version, never a password or secret env value.
    env_version = zerops_service_env.version.content
  }
}

# A trigger change restarts once; an unchanged apply performs no action.
# Restart starts a STOPPED service. Do not combine with desired_state = "STOPPED"
# unless you intend the resulting lifecycle drift. READY_TO_DEPLOY is rejected.
# Destroy is state-only and leaves the service running. Import is unsupported.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `service_id` (String)
- `triggers` (Map of String)

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) Operation timeouts. One timeout covers lock acquisition, API requests, queued work and readiness polling. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_restart` (String) Returned stack.restart process ID.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
